description:
tests/fixture_matrix.rs normalize_reported_line_number subtracts the FIXTURE's leading-comment-line count from every gutter number in the diagnostics text, regardless of which file that gutter line belongs to.

The sibling normalize_path_line_ref is correctly gated -- it only rewrites a line number when the line contains the fixture's own canonical_source_name. normalize_gutter_line_ref has no such gate: it matches any leading '<digits> |' and renumbers it.

CONSEQUENCE: warnings raised against runtime library sources (runtime:Enum.fz, runtime:List.fz, ...) get their snippet gutter renumbered by an offset that has nothing to do with them, and the offset CHANGES whenever the fixture's own comment header grows or shrinks. Editing prose in a fixture README therefore invalidates blessed diagnostics goldens for warnings in OTHER files.

OBSERVED (fz-66j, 2026-08-21): adding four comment lines to fixtures2/behavior/enum_list_allocations.fz shifted the runtime:Enum.fz snippet gutter from 227 to 223 while its own header stayed 'runtime:Enum.fz:267:3'. Header and gutter now disagree in every blessed golden of this kind -- enum_sort.expected.diagnostics has header 437 with gutter 379 (offset 58 = enum_sort's comment header length), map_enumerable and membership_operator likewise. The goldens are self-inconsistent by construction.

Verified NOT nondeterminism: five consecutive direct fz2 interp runs produce byte-identical stderr with the true gutter (267). The shift is introduced by the harness alone.

FIX: gate normalize_gutter_line_ref the same way normalize_path_line_ref is gated -- renumber a gutter line only while inside a snippet whose --> header names the fixture's own canonical source. Requires tracking the current snippet's file as the normalizer walks lines, since the gutter line does not itself carry a path. Re-bless the affected diagnostics goldens (currently 14 fixtures have expected.diagnostics; those citing runtime: sources are the affected set).

WHY IT MATTERS: the renumbering makes a blessed diagnostic golden depend on unrelated prose, and prints line numbers that do not exist in the file being cited -- a reader following runtime:Enum.fz:267 lands somewhere real, but the snippet above it claims 223.

comments.text:
CONCRETE INSTANCE, cost measured (fz-66j, 2026-08-21). fz-66j had to correct one sentence of prose in fixtures2/behavior/enum_sort.fz (it claimed 'ten protocol/control structs', which the fix made false). That three-line comment edit turned enum_sort RED on all three lanes and forced a re-bless of enum_sort.expected.diagnostics whose entire content is:

  379 -> 376   (runtime:Enum.fz split_sort_list snippet)
  391 -> 388   (runtime:Enum.fz merge_sort_lists snippet)

while the headers stayed at runtime:Enum.fz:437:3 and :449:3. A uniform -3 shift, exactly the number of comment lines added, applied to snippets in a file that was never touched.

This is the predicted failure mode observed end to end: a documentation edit required by CLAUDE.md ('documentation must be updated along with code') mechanically invalidates diagnostics goldens for warnings in OTHER files, and the resulting diff carries zero information about the program. It also cost a full 200s matrix cycle to discover, because blessing happened before the prose edit.

Raises this from cosmetic to a real tax on the doc-update rule: every fixture whose README length changes pays a golden re-bless plus a matrix cycle. Still P3, but the fix now has a measured justification.

title: fixture_matrix renumbers gutter line refs for FOREIGN files, so a fixture README edit silently shifts blessed runtime-library diagnostics
